def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    n_steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (n_steps - 1)  # seconds per step

    # Initialize arrays
    points = np.zeros((n_runs, n_steps, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, :2] = start  # lat, lon
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0       # seconds elapsed

    # Eastward ridge travel hypothesis: move roughly east (bearing 90 deg)
    # Add per-run small random perturbations to bearing for variation
    # Ridge walking tends to stay near high points: bias towards moving on higher elevation
    
    # Step distance tuned to produce median ~2.86 km in duration
    # Total target median dist = 2.86 km => average speed ~ 2.86km / (duration_s/3600)
    # walking ~1.4 m/s average for ridge walking (modulated by terrain)
    # Distance per step roughly: dt * speed (~1.4m/s), e.g., assuming 1.3 m/s average pace
    approx_speed_ms = 1.3
    dist_per_step = approx_speed_ms * dt  # meters per step

    # Bearings: base east (pi/2), jitter ±15 deg (in radians)
    base_bearing = np.pi / 2
    bearing_jitter = np.deg2rad(15)
    bearings = base_bearing + rng.uniform(-bearing_jitter, bearing_jitter, size=(n_runs, n_steps - 1))
    
    # Prepare arrays for lat/lon
    lat = np.full((n_runs,), start[0])
    lon = np.full((n_runs,), start[1])

    seconds_elapsed = np.zeros((n_runs,), dtype=float)

    # Precompute meters per degree for scaling approx linear moves
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon

    for step in range(1, n_steps):
        # Propose next points offset by dist_per_step along bearings[ :, step-1]
        # Use terrain.offset to compute next lat/lon
        next_lat, next_lon = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearings[:, step - 1], dist_per_step)

        # Clamp points to terrain box if outside, mark out-of-box later
        clamped_lat, clamped_lon = terrain.clamp(next_lat, next_lon)

        # Compute elevation difference and horizontal dist for Tobler speed calculation
        elev_curr = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        elev_next = terrain.elev(clamped_lat, clamped_lon)
        d_elev = elev_next - elev_curr
        d_horiz = dist_per_step

        speed_ms = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, d_horiz)  # vectorized speed in m/s

        # Adjust step distance to speed*dt to respect Tobler speed limiting downhill/uphill
        step_dist = speed_ms * dt
        # Recalculate offset for step_dist to refine lat/lon move
        refined_lat, refined_lon = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearings[:, step - 1], step_dist)

        # Clamp again to stay inside box
        refined_lat, refined_lon = terrain.clamp(refined_lat, refined_lon)

        # Update positions
        lat = refined_lat
        lon = refined_lon

        # Update times
        seconds_elapsed += dt

        points[:, step, 0] = lat
        points[:, step, 1] = lon
        points[:, step, 2] = seconds_elapsed

        # To keep walkers near ridges going east: shift bearing slightly toward higher elevation neighbors.
        # Sample 3 bearings around current bearing: base and ±10 deg, choose bearing with highest elev
        bearing_options = np.stack([
            bearings[:, step - 1] + np.deg2rad(d) for d in (0, -10, 10)
        ], axis=1)  # shape (n_runs,3)

        # For each option, estimate lat/lon at step_dist, get elevation
        lat_options = np.zeros_like(bearing_options)
        lon_options = np.zeros_like(bearing_options)

        for i in range(3):
            la, lo = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing_options[:, i], step_dist)
            la, lo = terrain.clamp(la, lo)
            lat_options[:, i] = la
            lon_options[:, i] = lo

        elev_options = terrain.elev(lat_options, lon_options)  # shape (n_runs,3)
        # Choose bearing leading to highest elevation point (ridge preference)
        best_idx = np.argmax(elev_options, axis=1)
        bearings[:, step - 1] = bearing_options[np.arange(n_runs), best_idx]

    # Check inside box for final points along all steps to determine ok
    inside_mask = terrain.inside(points[:, :, 0], points[:, :, 1])  # shape (n_runs, n_steps)
    ok = np.all(inside_mask, axis=1)

    return points, ok
